title: The number of past intermediate and transitional links was inconceivably great

fields.label: Label
fields.value: The number of past intermediate and transitional links was inconceivably great

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Because all living species are connected through extinct parent-species back to the common ancestor of each great class by steps no greater than those between varieties, the number of intermediate and transitional forms that have lived on earth must have been inconceivably great.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. IX: On the Imperfection of the Geological Record

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: So that the number of intermediate and transitional links, between all living and extinct species, must have been inconceivably great.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter IX, “On the Imperfection of the Geological Record”; section “On the nature of extinct intermediate varieties; on their number”. Scope: all living and extinct species

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch09-02: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.42

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Models can estimate missing diversity and transition counts for clades. The global magnitude and stipulated small phenotypic steps are not directly recoverable, and the key adjective is vague.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Estimate numbers and morphological spacing of unsampled ancestral lineages from dated phylogenies, fossil occurrence rates, and diversification models. Large inferred missing lineage counts support the qualitative claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
'Inconceivably great' has no numerical threshold.

Most extinct lineages and morphologies are unobserved.

fields.value:

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Public inventories can support order-of-magnitude diversity estimates, which is why data existence is fairly high, but the claim does not state a number that those estimates could miss. Because the result is entailed by gradualism once time is long, a large estimate does little to separate this sentence from its premise. This was one of the harder items to score because the rhetorical quantifier resists a decision rule.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Estimate cumulative species numbers through time from fossil occurrences and phylogenies and compare them with living richness and with described fossil species. A total vastly larger than the known record is consistent with the rhetoric; a reconstructed history with only modestly more links than living species would challenge it. No numerical cutoff defines 'inconceivably great'.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
'Inconceivably great' has no refuting threshold.

The number is largely a deduction from gradual steps plus deep time, so the test is partly circular.

Preservation bias dominates any estimate of true past diversity.
